subject: Urgent: sudden 429 spike / timeouts impacting Nestwell production
messages:
From: Alex Porter <alex.porter@nestwell.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, ops@nestwell.ai
Cc: security@nestwell.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: sudden 429 spike / timeouts impacting Nestwell production

Hi Soojin,

We just started seeing a large burst of 429s and timeouts across our production endpoints (~16:00 PDT). Latency is climbing and several background batch jobs started spamming retries which is making the situation worse. Impact: autocomplete and search features degrade for ~30% of our users.

I attached a small sample of logs showing 429 responses with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and a correlation id prefix nestwell-6f. We need urgent help — can you confirm whether this is a rate-limit change on your side or some misconfiguration in how our org/project tiers are mapped?

We are pausing the heaviest jobs but need a short-term mitigation if this is a Redwood-side quota. Pls escalate — CISO is copied because they want to understand if any customer data is affected.

Attachments: nestwell_429_sample_logs.zip

Thanks,
Alex Porter
Head of Platform
Nestwell AI
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Porter <alex.porter@nestwell.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden 429 spike / timeouts impacting Nestwell production

Alex — thanks for the quick heads up and for the logs. Im escalating to SRE/ops right now (Aditya, Jonas). Apologies for the disruption; were treating this as P1.

Immediate next steps:
- I have attached the rateplan matrix (redwood_rateplan_matrix.csv) and our incident playbook.
- Aditya / Jonas: can you confirm whether Nestwells org->project tier mapping was changed or rolled back in the last 24h? If this is a tiering misroute well need to patch the service that selects effective limits.
- Alex: please continue to hold heavy batch runs and reduce retry multiplier if possible; that will reduce pressure while we triage.

I will keep you updated every 30–45 minutes.

— Soojin
SoojIn Lee
Enterprise Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: sudden 429 spike / timeouts impacting Nestwell production

Forwarding Alex's logs. Summary: customer seeing a spike in 429s; they observe X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0. Hypothesis from initial read: an org-level limit was accidentally applied at the project-level for Nestwell, causing token-level rate budgeting to over-apply and fallback to 429s when tiering logic tries to map org->project quotas. This could cascade into retry storms because clients are retrying with exponential backoff incorrectly configured.

What I need from SRE:
- Quick confirm whether the effective limit for Nestwell's projects dropped around 16:00 PDT.
- If yes, can we temporarily lift the effective per-project limit or enable the older fallback path?
- Any quick config we can flip to break the retry storm loop (e.g., alter Retry-After headers or inject short-lived soft-bucket)?

Attaching: redwood_rateplan_matrix.csv and playbook_retry_storm.md for context.

Thanks — Soojin
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, alex.porter@nestwell.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: sudden 429 spike / timeouts impacting Nestwell production

On Sun, Oct 11, 2026 at 4:28 PM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Forwarding Alex's logs. Summary: customer seeing a spike in 429s; they observe X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0. Hypothesis from initial read: an org-level limit was accidentally applied at the project-level for Nestwell, causing token-level rate budgeting to over-apply and fallback to 429s when tiering logic tries to map org->project quotas. This could cascade into retry storms because clients are retrying with exponential backoff incorrectly configured.

Confirmed — we see the same in internal metrics (incidents/INC-2026-8932). Root cause: an automated migration task that applied quota tier updates to "project" rows instead of "org" rows for a small set of enterprise accounts. Nestwell's project entries were left with a legacy low limit (250 req/min) while their org-level reserved capacity (10k req/min) was not being consulted due to a tier lookup regression. That created an effective drop in available capacity at ~15:58 PDT, which lines up with the customer's window.

Immediate mitigations were enacting (15:58–now):
- Hotfix rolled to the tiering lookup service to prefer org-level caps when project-level entry is flagged as "legacy". Deploy completed at 17:00 PDT.
- Temporary increase to Nestwell's project limit to 5k req/min (manual override) — live at 17:10 PDT.
- Adjusted Retry-After behavior for affected endpoints to return 10s instead of immediate 0, to reduce retry amplification.

Follow-ups (next 24h):
- Patch to migration task to prevent re-writing project rows (in code review).
- Postmortem and cross-check of other enterprise accounts for similar misapplied migrations.

ETA: customers should see a material drop in 429s within 30 minutes of the manual override. I'm keeping the manual override in place until the migration patch is hardened.

Aditya
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: incident dashboard (https://app.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-8932)
From: Alex Porter <alex.porter@nestwell.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: security@nestwell.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 17:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden 429 spike / timeouts impacting Nestwell production

Thanks Aditya — that matches what we see. After you put the override in place our errors dropped from ~18% to ~2% over the last 15 minutes. Were unpausing lower-priority jobs at throttled rates and will keep heavy jobs paused for another hour.

Two quick asks:
1) Can we get a short-term credit for the production impact window? Were tracking user-facing errors in our SLOs and this will hit our business reporting.
2) Can you share the timeline and a short plain-English summary we can give to our security and compliance team? Theyre cc'd.

Alex

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Porter <alex.porter@nestwell.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, security@nestwell.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden 429 spike / timeouts impacting Nestwell production

Alex — really glad to hear error rates dropped. Summary & next steps (for your ops and security teams):

Plain-English summary: at ~15:58 PDT an automated quota migration incorrectly wrote new limits to project-level entries for a small set of customers including Nestwell. When the tiering lookup encountered those rows it treated them as authoritative, which caused per-project effective limits to be much lower than the org-reserved capacity. That produced a sudden drop in allowed throughput and resulted in 429s. The client-side retries amplified the user-visible errors.

What we did:
- 16:00–17:00 PDT: triage and confirmation.
- 17:00 PDT: deployed hotfix to tiering lookup service to prefer org-level caps for flagged legacy project rows.
- 17:10 PDT: manual interim override increased Nestwell project limit to 5k req/min; adjusted Retry-After to 10s on affected endpoints.
- Ongoing: patch to migration task (code review), account sweep for other affected customers, postmortem to be shared within 72 hours.

Short-term credit: Marissa (cc'd) will coordinate a goodwill credit for the Nestwell incident window; we'll get you a proposed credit amount by EOD.

Immediate request for Nestwell: please share any additional log slices if you still see anomalous correlation ids. Well keep the manual override until the migration patch is in production.

Incident link: https://app.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-8932
Postmortem delivery: targeted within 72 hours.

Thanks again for quick coordination.

— Soojin Lee
Enterprise Success Manager, Redwood Inference
